summary: Jong Cheol Lee works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Seoul National University and earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima in 1994, later holding posts at the University of Mysore and the Academy of Korean Studies.

Jong-Nam Choi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under the supervision of Lambert Schmithausen.

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and the University of California, Los Angeles, where he earned an MA in 1994. He served as associate professor at the Academy of Korean Studies.

Jos Gommans specializes in South Asian history and Indology. He studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan Heesterman and André Wink, later holding posts at the Dutch Research Council, Kern Institute, and Leiden University.

Josef Horovitz worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He completed his doctorate under Eduard Sachau around 1895–1898 and held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt from circa 1914 to 1931.

Josef Schick was a linguist who studied at Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he earned his PhD in 1889 under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich (1896–1925).

Josef Strzygowski was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the University of Munich. He held posts at the University of Graz (1892–1909), the University of Vienna (1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University (1925–1926).
Josef van Ess worked in religious studies. He studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1953 to 1959 and held a post at the University of Tübingen from circa 1968 to 1999.

Joseph Campbell specialized in religious studies and Indology. Educated at Columbia, Paris, and Munich, he earned his BA and MA under William Witherle Lawrence at Columbia, later teaching at Canterbury School and Sarah Lawrence College (1934–1972).
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at McGill University, attested in 2004, where he studied under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Joseph E. Schwartzberg was an Indologist and historical geographer who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hartshorne. He held positions at the University of Pennsylvania, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Minnesota (1964–2000).

Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at University College School and the University of London, he served as President of Harris Manchester College, Oxford, and held a post at the University of Oxford.

Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. Educated at Columbia University, he studied under numerous traditional Buddhist teachers, taught at Naropa University in 1974, and co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Joseph Hackin was a scholar of archaeology, Central Asian studies, and Buddhism. He studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, directing the Musée Guimet, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and DAFA.

Joseph Haroutunian was a religious studies scholar. He studied at the American University of Beirut, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia University, holding academic appointments at Wellesley College, McCormick Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Kitagawa specialized in religious studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Rikkyo University and earned his PhD under Joachim Wach at the University of Chicago, where he spent his career and served as Dean of the Divinity School.

Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche. He served as a visiting scholar at Columbia University and founded the Nalanda Institute.

Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who completed an MA at Columbia University around 1948–1950. He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University, where his appointment was noted in 1991.

Joseph A. Marino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox, and held an assistant professor post there, attested in 2026.

Joseph Needham was a historian and sinologist educated at Oundle School and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge. He spent his career at the University of Cambridge, serving as Master of Gonville and Caius and Director of the Needham Research Institute.
